rgraphtool

rgraphtool is a standalone native R/C++ port of the Python graph-tool network analysis library (originally developed by Tiago P. Peixoto). It embeds graph-tool’s C++ adjacency data structure (boost::adj_list) and ports its Bayesian network inference, reconstruction, layout, visualization, and C++ extension interfaces directly to R with no Python runtime dependency.

All exact model description lengths, negative log-likelihoods, and incremental MCMC updates are numerically verified to machine precision (< 1e-11) against a pinned graph-tool 3.9 reference build.

Installation

rgraphtool requires R with a C++23-capable compiler, plus the Rcpp and BH (>= 1.81.0) packages. Optional packages ggplot2 and svglite enable ggplot_graph() and dependency-free SVG export.

# From a local checkout:
install.packages(".", repos = NULL, type = "source")

# Or from GitHub using remotes / pak:
# remotes::install_github("diogro/rgraphtool")

Note: rgraphtool uses portable C++23 std::thread parallelism (no libomp required on macOS) and requires a C++23-capable toolchain.

Quick start

1. Creating graphs & edge properties 

library(rgraphtool)

g <- graph_create(4L, directed = TRUE)
graph_add_edges(
  g,
  rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3), c(3, 1), c(2, 4)),
  properties = list(weight = c(1.2, 0.8, 2.5, 1.0))
)
graph_num_vertices(g)          # 4
graph_num_edges(g)             # 4
graph_degree(g, "out")         # 1 2 1 0
graph_edge_property(g, "weight")

Vertex IDs are 1-based. Parallel edges and self-loops are supported. Graphs are mutable external-pointer objects (process-local; store edge tables separately if saving to disk with saveRDS()).

2. Hierarchical SBM inference & posterior sampling 

# Load any network from Netzschleuder (https://networks.skewed.de)
celegans <- netzschleuder_network("celegansneural")

set.seed(42)
fit <- minimize_nested_blockmodel_dl(celegans$graph)
fit
plot_hierarchy(fit)

# Posterior MCMC sampling and partition mode clustering
samples <- sample_posterior(fit, nsamples = 100L, burnin = 50L, thin = 5L)
modes <- mode_cluster_state(samples)
mode_summary(modes)

3. Network reconstruction from dynamics 

# Reconstruct an interaction graph directly from equilibrium Ising spins
g_true <- graph_create(20L, directed = FALSE)
graph_add_edges(g_true, rbind(cbind(1:19, 2:20), c(20L, 1L)))

set.seed(1)
spins <- simulate_ising(g_true, weights = 0.6, n_samples = 400L)
st <- pseudo_ising_block_state(spins, nested = TRUE)
rec <- reconstruct_dynamics(st, niter = 20L)
rec

4. Layouts, animations, interactive views & maps 

set.seed(7)
pos <- sfdp_layout(g_true)
plot_graph(g_true, pos = pos, edge_curve = 0.12, axes = TRUE,
           output = tempfile(fileext = ".pdf"))

# Standalone zero-dependency HTML5 Canvas animations & interactive BFS explorer
animate_sirs(g_true, pos = pos, n_steps = 60L, mode = "html", open = TRUE)
interactive_bfs(g_true, pos = pos, max_dist = 3L, mode = "html", open = TRUE)

Multi-threading for large networks

rgraphtool includes a portable header-only C++23 thread pool (src/parallel.h) that works across macOS, Linux, and Windows without requiring OpenMP:

rgraphtool_max_threads()
rgraphtool_set_num_threads(4L)
# Or via global option:
options(rgraphtool.nthreads = 4L)

Writing C++ extensions

User C++ extensions and downstream R packages (LinkingTo: rgraphtool, Rcpp, BH) can #include <rgraphtool.h> for zero-copy access to rgraphtool::Graph, range-based graph iteration (vertices_range, edges_range, out_edges_range, in_edges_range, all_edges_range, out_neighbors_range, in_neighbors_range, all_neighbors_range), and vertex/edge property maps with bounds-checked defaults and upfront-validated zero-overhead unchecked access (.get_unchecked()):

# Compile and run a bundled standalone C++ extension via Rcpp::sourceCpp()
compile_cpp_extension(rgraphtool_extension_example("kcore"))
ext_kcore_decomposition(g, checked = FALSE)

See ?cpp_extensions and demo("cpp_extensions", package = "rgraphtool") for complete examples and benchmarks.

Validation against graph-tool 3.9

tools/reference/ contains a pinned pixi environment with the conda-forge build of graph-tool 3.9 (b24bc428e8426d0acb36b2d57bd61633335a3a26) along with the scripts used to generate numerical reference fixtures for the test suite (1,272 tests). Python is never required to install, use, or test rgraphtool.

Attribution and license

rgraphtool is derived from graph-tool release 3.9 by Tiago P. Peixoto. Vendored adjacency headers reside in inst/include/rgraphtool/vendor/ with their original copyright notices intact (unused generated config.h includes were removed from two supporting headers).
